"Calling in the Reserves" is a Horde courier task entrusted to adventurers resting at Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder sends you south to the edge of the Barrens with orders to relieve an exhausted sentry watching the Great Lift.

Even in an era of relative prosperity following the Third War, maintaining garrisons across central Kalimdor tests the Horde's resources. At Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains, Maggran Earthbinder oversees logistics and troop welfare. Recognizing that seasoned soldiers wear thin under endless watch duty, Maggran dispatches a letter of reassignment south to the Great Lift, where a young sentry named Grish Longrunner has been standing guard far from home.

The Great Lift serves as the singular engineering artery linking the high plateaus of the southern Barrens down into the wind-carved canyons of Thousand Needles. Handing the letter over to Grish relieves him of an isolated and monotonous watch over the lift mechanisms, clearing the way for him to finally return to his family and allowing fresh reserves to step in.

Cloth and Leather Armor is an errand commissioned by Marshal Dughan in Goldshire. Impressed by an adventurer's service, Dughan issues an official military armor marker redeemable with local artisan Sara Timberlain. This task directs recruits east past Guard Thomas's bridge into the Eastvale Logging Camp to obtain proper gear for the defense of the realm.

Guard Thomas stands vigil at the eastern crossing over the river in Elwynn, holding the border against hostile murlocs and roving gnolls. When a capable traveler carries his report to Goldshire, Marshal Dughan rewards that service with an official Stormwind Armor Marker rather than pulling equipment from the garrison's own meager stores. This marker acts as a military requisition voucher, officially recognizing the bearer's service to the crown.

Across the bridge to the east lies the Eastvale Logging Camp, Elwynn's primary timber operation. Working out of the settlement, Sara Timberlain holds an official commission from the Stormwind Army to produce cloth and leather gear. Because the kingdom's centralized armories are strained and stretched thin, local artisans like Sara are vital for outfitting troops and auxiliary scouts on the frontier.

A Rogue's Deal is a confrontation with Calvin Montague in Deathknell. After offering work to newly awakened Forsaken with the promise of wealth, the sly rogue's true intentions come to light when payment is demanded.

Calvin Montague loiters near the crypts of Deathknell offering seemingly easy work for newly risen Forsaken. Claiming there is good coin to be earned by delivering a letter, Montague sends green adventurers into danger. However, once the errand is done, Montague conveniently forgets his promise of payment, feigning utter ignorance about any arrangement or owed coin.

When pressed to honor his bargain, Montague shows his true colors. Rather than parting with his silver, he draws his weapons, betting that he can easily cut down an inexperienced fledgling. Beating sense into the rogue forces him to concede. Thoroughly battered, he coughs up a cut of coin, freely admitting that he lied about the payout simply because he thought he could get away with it.

Moonglade is an introductory rite of passage for young night elf druids learning to commune with the sacred lands of Kalimdor. Guided by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, novices learn the spell to magically transport themselves across the world into Moonglade to meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. This marks the beginning of their spiritual journey toward mastering the strength of the bear form.

Moonglade stands apart from the rest of Azeroth as an ancient sanctuary dedicated to the teachings of Cenarius. Under the watchful stewardship of Keeper Remulos, its tranquil groves provide peace and deep communion with nature. For a young druid, learning to project one's spirit across the land into Moonglade via the teleportation spell is a critical step, granting constant access to the heart of druidic wisdom regardless of mortal distances.

While Moonglade is open to all who walk the path of the wild, it is not free of tension. A growing rift divides Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus and Keeper Remulos in Moonglade over the stewardship of nature and the creation of Teldrassil. Despite these philosophical fractures within the Cenarion Circle, young acolytes are still welcomed unconditionally into the haven of Nighthaven to pursue their sacred studies.

Arriving in Nighthaven brings the novice before Dendrite Starblaze, an elder tasked with guiding fledglings along the ways of the Claw. Before any initiate can claim the mantle of the bear, they must be immersed in its perspective: endurance, fury, and unyielding defense of the wild. Starblaze receives each new student with reverent deference to Father Cenarius, commencing the trials of the Great Bear Spirit.

Teleporting to Moonglade connects a druid directly to the heart of their order. Because training, communion with spirits, and high-level council take place in Nighthaven, having an instantaneous spiritual conduit ensures every practitioner can return to study and replenish their spiritual energies.

Having overindulged on his own potent brew and slept through his watch, Foggy entrusts an Alliance traveler with rushing a fresh batch to Hillsbrad to settle a lingering debt with Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore.

Life on watch atop the shattered Thandol Span is wet, cold, and notoriously dull. Foggy MacKreel manages the damp chill by imbibing his own homemade moonshine, a concoction so fierce he compares its aftermath to an entire brigade of siege engines rolling across his skull. Unfortunately for Foggy, one drink too many caused him to pass out during his shift. With Longbraid the Grim commanding the dwarves defending the Span, Foggy cannot afford any further lapses in discipline.

Compounding Foggy's troubles is a longstanding debt owed to Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore. Foggy promised Bilger a batch of his personal brew to balance the books, but between his hangover and his shift duties, he finds himself minutes away from default. Relying on gryphons and swift feet, travelers must race across the Arathi Highlands to Southshore to deliver the jug before Bilger decides Foggy has skipped out on his tab once again.

Foggy MacKreel is a dwarf found on the broken part of the Thandol Span, reached from the Arathi Highlands side. Known for brewing extremely stout homemade moonshine, he tends to sample his own product a little too freely while on duty.

Why is this delivery so urgent?

Foggy ran severely behind schedule after passing out drunk during his watch. He has a strict deadline to deliver the moonshine to Brewmeister Bilger to settle an overdue tab, leaving barely a quarter of an hour to make the journey from the Thandol Span to Southshore.

Brewmeister Bilger is a master dwarven brewer who plies his trade in the coastal settlement of Southshore within the Hillsbrad Foothills. He appreciates stout alcohol and has an outstanding business agreement with Foggy MacKreel.

How does one get the moonshine to Southshore in time?

There is no boat from the Span to Southshore. The quickest route is to head into the Arathi Highlands and take a gryphon from Refuge Pointe to Southshore if you know that flight path, then find Brewmeister Bilger in town before the timer expires.
